verdicts.flaw_description: Uncontrolled co-intervention: "The lubricant supply moved from mineral to synthetic grade mid-cycle, and every machine here drew from that supply." A grease upgrade is itself a strong determinant of bearing life, it changed at the same time as the bearing swap, and it hit 100 percent of the measured machines, so the extra 260-410 hours cannot be attributed to the bearing design rather than the lubricant. Nothing in the report separates the two.

Measured area does not match treated area: "Yields cover every hectare in each block fitted with the line, and the line watered about a quarter of each block's hectares intermittently." The yield-per-hectare figures are averaged over whole blocks of which only roughly a quarter of the hectares actually received the drip line, and even those only intermittently, so a block-wide 0.4-0.7 t/ha rise is mostly generated by land the intervention never touched. The measurement unit and the treatment unit are different populations.

The outcome is measured before the treatment in three of the four plots: "fed 3 August, measured by 20 June", "fed 2 May, measured by 19 April", and "fed 24 November, measured by 7 October". Only the fern (fed 8 January, measured 26 February) has the measurement after the feed. A height recorded weeks before the fertilizer was applied cannot have been caused by it, so the reported gains are temporally impossible as evidence for the claim.

Uncontrolled simultaneous change: "The free trial ran eighteen days, up from ten in the earlier period, and every cohort here signed up on that trial." Week-two retention is exactly the window the trial length governs - at day 14 the new cohorts are still inside a free trial while the comparison cohorts had already been dropped out of one - and every measured cohort was on the longer trial, so the 3-6 point lift is fully confounded with the trial extension rather than with the onboarding email.

Treatment was not actually delivered to a quarter of the measured group: "Averages cover every patient put on the protocol, and a quarter of each intake let the home exercises lapse." This also contradicts the opening line that these are intakes "that completed the same physiotherapy protocol". The averages therefore describe a population a quarter of which did not receive the protocol as defined, so the abduction gains are not attributable to a protocol those patients did not complete.

Exposure does not match measurement: "Scores cover every pupil on each class roll, and a quarter of each roll missed at least one program session." The 5-9 point comprehension gain is computed over full class rolls, a quarter of which did not receive the complete program, so the reported score change is not a measurement of the program as delivered and the report gives no breakdown separating attenders from non-attenders.

Survivorship selection in the outcome set: "Only runs completed end to end on the issued route entered the timing set, and drivers at each depot abandoned the issued route on roughly one run in six." The one-in-six runs where the new route was abandoned - precisely the runs likely to have gone badly or run long - are excluded from the timings, while the comparison period presumably includes all its runs. That filtering alone can produce an apparent 5-9 minute improvement with no real effect from the routing change.

Non-compliers are dropped from the numbers: "Absence figures cover the pupils on the revised timetable throughout, and about a fifth of each cohort spent weeks on the old timetable." Roughly 20 percent of each cohort is excluded from the absence figures, and pupils who spent weeks off the revised timetable are plausibly the frequently-absent ones, so the 4-7 percent drop can be an artefact of removing the worst attenders from the measured group rather than an effect of the timetable change.
